title: Commitment Mapper: staged spillback orchestration and data-boundary-aware throughput commitments
creator: Liam Chen
description:
Summary: Build a Commitment Mapper service and orchestration layer that binds customer throughput commitments to zone-level reservations while enabling a staged spillback (soft failover) when zones are degraded. The mapper must be data-boundary-aware: it enforces data residency constraints (regional vs. zonal) and ensures no request is routed to a zone that violates residency policy during normal operation or failover.

Problem: Today Dedicated pools are allocated at a coarse granularity and failover is binary (drain/evacuate). Customers with residency constraints experience either full capacity loss or complex manual work to preserve locality. We need predictable soft-degradation semantics: guarantee committed throughput with minimal latency impact and controlled spillback when local zones are constrained.

Goals:
- Map customer-level throughput commitments (tokens/sec, concurrent inference units) to per-zone reservations with priority lanes.
- Orchestrate staged spillback: gradual redirection of traffic to adjacent zones/regions in defined increments rather than immediate global failover.
- Enforce data residency: all spillback routes must be validated against customer's residency contract (region-only, zone-preferred, strict-sovereign).
- Provide deterministic billing/SLAs visibility: customers see how committed throughput is preserved across the staging windows and how costs change when spillback occurs.
- Integrate with autoscaler and prewarm agents so soft-spillback triggers prewarm requests and avoids cold-start latency spikes.

Out of scope: full cross-region DB replication; long-running stateful model migrations.

Design overview: Commitment Mapper is a control-plane microservice that consumes: customer contracts (commitments), real-time fleet telemetry (utilization per-zone), and residency policy rules. It produces zone reservation plans and a spillback schedule for each affected customer. The runtime agent (runtime-orchestrator) subscribes to plans and performs incremental traffic shifts: stepwise percentage moves with adjustable ramp windows. The mapper includes a safety policy engine that blocks any plan step that would violate residency constraints or exceed allowed latency degradation.

Key APIs to add:
- POST /commitments/apply -> creates/updates commitment mapping (input: commitment id, target capacity, residency policy, preference tags)
- GET /commitments/{id}/plan -> returns current per-zone reservation plan and spillback schedule
- POST /commitments/{id}/force-evacuate -> admin path for urgent full failover with audit

Telemetry and metrics:
- commitment.reserved_tokens_per_zone (gauge)
- commitment.effective_throughput_preserved (percent)
- commitment.spillback_stage (0..N)
- commitment.spillback_latency_impact_p50/p95 (ms)
- commitment.residency_violations.blocked (counter)

Operational interfaces: dashboards in Console-ops for per-customer commitment health, a staged spillback timeline visualization, and per-zone reservation summaries. Alerts: when effective_throughput_preserved < 90% for > 5m for P0 contracts.
acceptance_criteria: Commitment Mapper service exists and accepts POST /commitments/apply with validation of residency policy.
Runtime-orchestrator implements staged spillback and honors per-step ramp windows; validated in canary with synthetic load.
No residency policy is bypassed during staging; automated tests and negative tests show blocked steps when policy would be violated.
Dashboards show reserved_tokens_per_zone and effective_throughput_preserved for sample customers.
Autoscaler integration: prewarm requests are issued before each ramp stage and cold-start rate < 2% during failover tests.
Billing/usage reporting maps capacity shifts to cost buckets and changes are visible in customer console under committed usage.
Runbook created with step-by-step mitigation for failed staged spillbacks and an admin force-evacuate path linked to an audit log.
Security review completed and approval noted in ticket comments.
implementation_notes: Phase 1 (MVP): control-plane mapper + runtime subscription; simple two-stage spillback (local -> neighbor -> region).
Phase 2: extend to multi-stage percent ramps, cost-aware routing (prefer cheaper model variant on spillback), and policy templates for enterprise contracts.
Mapper stores plans in durable config-store (use existing configdb partition for dedicated capacity). Avoid embedding heavy state in mapper; runtime agents keep ephemeral state for in-flight ramping.
Use existing tagging system to mark zone affinity, sovereign regions, and preferred lanes. Add 'residency_allowlist' and 'hard_residency' flags per commitment.
Autoscaler changes: new event hooks for prewarm_token_request and prewarm_complete; add backpressure signal to avoid over-allocating in neighbor zones.
Performance: mapper must compute plans in <200ms for a single commitment update in normal cases; batch recompute for large-scale incidents.
Fail-safes: if telemetry disconnects, runtime should default to conservative plan (no spillback) and page SRE for manual intervention.
Compliance: ensure audit logs record every spillback step and the identity that authorized it (system vs. operator).
migration_plan: 1) Add API and config schema; create v1 commitments for a small pilot of 3 customers.
2) Wire runtime-orchestrator subscription and test staged spillback in isolated canary region (eu-west-1).
3) Enable prewarm integration and run soak tests for 48h under synthetic traffic patterns simulating zone degradation.
4) Expand pilot to 15 customers across two regions and gather telemetry for cost/latency impact.
5) Full rollout with feature-flag gate and ops runbook.
runbook: Immediate steps on alert: 1) verify telemetry, 2) pause next ramp stage via /commitments/{id}/plan PATCH, 3) trigger prewarm to neighbor zone if cold-starts observed, 4) open incident if > 10% throughput loss after staging window.
Admin forcible evacuation: only via POST /commitments/{id}/force-evacuate and must include justification; audit entry required.
Rollback: revert to previous committed plan and redeploy runtime orchestration at previous tag if new runtime agent misbehaves.
